objective: Add a wall-time excursion rule to the monitor: flag any run beyond 10 times its solver's running 99th percentile, stop and investigate beyond 100 times
rationale: Mined from the mega-batch ledger: solver wall times are tightly banded, with the cylinder at median 3.7 seconds and 99th percentile 19.7 seconds and the wing at median 5.8 seconds and 99th percentile 8.6 seconds, yet three runs per solver recorded wall times near 16300 seconds, over 800 times the 99th percentile, and every one was recorded ok with no anomaly anywhere. A hung or starved run that eventually returns a plausible number is invisible to every current check. The rule keeps the excursion as a named field on the record so fleet learning can separate solver cost from infrastructure stalls.
expected_knowledge_gain: The fleet ledger stops silently absorbing 800-fold wall-time excursions, and the cost model behind mission planning stops being polluted by infrastructure stalls counted as solver time
outcome: In force, and the retrospective assessment it made possible has been generated over all 208,193 ledger rows: 19 rows would have been flagged and 11 called fatal, and every one of the 30 was recorded ok at the time with nothing flagged, because the rule did not exist yet. The six worst are the six runs near 16,300 seconds on 2026-07-23 and 2026-07-24, at 1,047 to 2,214 times their own solver's 99th percentile, judged against an envelope learned from that same ledger: cylinder p99 15.23 s over 69,288 runs, wing p99 7.37 s over 69,149. Closing the item caught a second defect, in the rule itself: check_wall_time carried its own literal 20.0 for five days after the shared constant had been corrected to the approved 10.0, so every caller taking the default was judging on a threshold nobody approved. The assessment is labelled an assessment throughout and rewrites no row.
